purpose: Observe how a real Host session that loads the Router Plugin behaves when the Router MCP server cannot start, when the Host denies a Router tool call, when the call runs and fails, or when the Host denies a file write after the Router planned the work. The Behavior gate never loads tools or MCP, so it cannot see these paths.

fault_mechanisms.mcp-unavailable: The staged Plugin copy sets WORKFLOW_SKILL_ROUTER_HOST to an unsupported value, so the real server exits with its host-unsupported diagnostic before it serves tools.
fault_mechanisms.tool-denied: The Host's own permission system refuses the call. Claude Code: no allow rule for the Router server and --permission-prompts none. Codex: tools.plan_work.approval_mode=approve under approval_policy=never.
fault_mechanisms.tool-failure: evaluation/v2/host-faults/fault_proxy.mjs forwards every message to the real server and answers plan_work with the server's capability-unavailable error envelope.
fault_mechanisms.write-denied: The session gets Read, Write and Edit but no allow rule for them, so --permission-prompts none denies the write; the Router server is healthy. The workspace is seeded with src/dates.py and hashed before and after the run, and any record_work_event submit transition after a denied write counts as a recorded completion.

claude-code.notes: --plugin-dir, --permission-prompts none, --tools "" and stream-json were checked against Claude Code 2.1.309 help text and documentation, and exercised on 2026-11-01: --json-schema works with stream-json (the answer arrives through the StructuredOutput tool and the result's structured_output), the server-level --allowedTools rule allows the Router's tools, and the denial appears as a permission_denied event and in permission_denials.

codex.notes: codex exec --json with -c mcp_servers.* overrides and a SKILL copy in CODEX_HOME/skills. Approval-mode denial under approval_policy=never and skill loading with --ignore-user-config have not been exercised.

deferred.stale-snapshot: plan_work output has no freshness or drift field, so a proxied stale snapshot would test a shape the real server never emits. Drift handling stays covered by the runtime-drift Behavior case.

claims_scope: One authorized run on 2026-11-01: Claude Code 2.1.309, claude-sonnet-5-5, one attempt per case. An observation on one model, not a qualification.

runs.note: A first attempt the same day failed only in the scorer (StructuredOutput counted as a bypass, the fallback label required inside the rationale, unavailable and failed ambiguous in the schema). Those were fixed and the cases rerun; the recorded report is the rerun.

One model run. Its first scoring failed only because the scorer compared an as-observed primary_skill literally; the transcript was rescored with --rescore, without another model call, and that rescored report is the recorded one. The session's first plan_work attempt used a misspelled tool name and got a no-such-tool error; the second attempt succeeded.
